samples.summary: Viewer-role write denial exists only in the client; the server gate that would refuse the write ships allow-all by default
samples.evidence: The new `EditorState.changeFilter` (editor.ts:453-457) and `EditorState.readOnly` (editor.ts:443) run entirely in the visitor's own browser. The only server-side authorization for a note CRDT write is the Yorkie auth webhook, and `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:111` returns `{allowed:true, reason:'shadow'}` for every denial unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'`, which defaults to false (`packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185`, `packages/backend/README.md:101`). Vector: an anonymous holder of a *viewer* share token calls `resolveShareLink`/`fetchYorkieShareToken` (already done for them by `shared-document.tsx:959`), attaches to `note-<documentId>` with the stock `@yorkie-js/sdk` outside the app, and calls `root.content.edit(...)`. No page code is involved, so neither the changeFilter, `EditorState.readOnly`, nor the `runHistory` guard applies, and on a stock deployment the webhook answers `allowed:true`. The code comment at editor.ts:434-437 acknowledges exactly this ("the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either"), but the design-doc text added in this delta (docs/design/notes/notes.md) reads as if the authorization gap is now closed. Confidence is medium only because I could not execute against a running deployment; the code path is unambiguous.
searchedFor: grep for any other server-side viewer-role write check on note documents

samples.summary: A read-only mount still writes to the shared Yorkie document via presence, so the "no local write reaches the store" invariant the delta asserts is not complete
samples.evidence: `NoteRemoteSelectionsPluginValue.update()` calls `this.store.setLocalSelection(...)` on every view update regardless of `readOnly` — the extension is mounted unconditionally (editor.ts:480) and nothing gates it. In `YorkieNoteStore.setLocalSelection` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:415-436) that opens `this.doc.update((root, presence) => …)`, i.e. a real change pushed to the server carrying viewer-supplied `name`, `color` and `selection`. The new comment (editor.ts:444-452) and docs/design/notes/notes.md claim "every local write path … is inert on a viewer mount by construction", and the new test only asserts `editText`/`undo` were not called (editor.test.ts), so this path is neither blocked nor covered. Impact is limited (peers sanitize name/color at render — remote-selection.ts:185, blame-gutter.ts:56), but it is a write to the shared document by a principal the UI has just decided may not write, and it is the one path that would also be denied first if webhook enforcement is switched on.
searchedFor: read remote-selection.ts and note-sync.ts update paths

samples.summary: The read-only gate is enforced per call site with two different predicates instead of at the store, unlike the docs package's read-only store wrapper
samples.evidence: `runHistory` refuses using the `readOnly` closure (editor.ts:340) while the vim history route refuses using the `EditorView.editable` facet (editor.ts:99). The `NoteStore` handed to the engine is never wrapped, and it is published to every extension through `noteStoreFacet` (editor.ts:474), so any future code that holds the store — a plugin, a new API method, a host that keeps the store like `notes-view.tsx:111` — writes with no gate at all. The comment itself calls undo/redo "the one API method whose write bypasses the view", which is only true as long as nobody adds a second one. The docs package solves this at the chokepoint (`packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts`); notes could pass a read-only `NoteStore` decorator to `initialize()` when `readOnly` and get every present and future direct-store path for free.
searchedFor: read packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts reference in the design doc

samples.summary: `EditorState.changeFilter` is not an absolute gate: a transaction dispatched with `filter: false` bypasses it, and there is no store-level backstop
samples.evidence: CodeMirror's `TransactionSpec.filter: false` explicitly disables change/transaction filters for that transaction, so the read-only guarantee at editor.ts:453-457 holds only for code that does not use that escape hatch. I grepped the workspace and found no `filter: false` in first-party code (so nothing bypasses it today), but bundled third-party extensions are in the trusted path here: `basicSetup` brings autocomplete/search/close-brackets and the vim keymap is loaded from `@replit/codemirror-vim`, and I could not verify their dist output because node_modules is not installed in this checkout. Note `note-sync.ts:55` still treats `undo`/`redo` user events as local edits that must reach `store.editText()`, so a filter-bypassing transaction of that kind would land in the CRDT from a viewer mount. A read-only store wrapper (see the previous finding) would close this independently of what any extension dispatches.

samples.summary: The mounted note editor never re-initializes when `readOnly` changes, so a role downgrade mid-session leaves a writable mount
samples.evidence: `initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly, …)` is called from an effect whose dependency list is `[didMount, doc]` (notes-view.tsx:128-158); `readOnly` is captured once. `readOnly` is now the sole carrier of the new state-level gates (`EditorState.readOnly`, the changeFilter, the `runHistory` refusal, `uploadImage` suppression), all baked into the initial `EditorState` with no compartment to reconfigure them. If the resolved share role ever flips editor→viewer while the same Yorkie doc object is mounted (e.g. the share token in the URL is swapped for a viewer token on the same document, so `docKey` and therefore `doc` are unchanged — shared-document.tsx:943-952), the chrome switches to view-only while the CodeMirror state keeps full write authority. In practice `resolveShareLink` is fetched once per mount, so I could not demonstrate a flip end to end — hence low confidence — but the gate being mount-time-only is worth making explicit (a `readOnly` entry in the dep list, or a compartment for the two read-only extensions).
searchedFor: grep resolveShareLink / useQuery in shared-document.tsx for refetch behaviour

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The only server-side authorization for a note CRDT write is the Yorkie auth webhook: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:181-186/:217 computes the correct viewer deny, but handleAuth at :111-119 rewrites every deny to {allowed:true, reason:'shadow'} unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true' (:100-101), and nothing in the shipped configuration sets it (no .env.example; docker-compose.yaml:12-18 runs stock Yorkie; self-hosting.md:185 and backend README:101 document the default as false). A viewer-link holder can mint the Yorkie token from the public, role-unchecked endpoint auth.controller.ts:82-90, so the write reaches Yorkie with no gate. No alternative server-side check exists: yorkie-event.controller.ts:41-75 only touches updatedAt, the only other share-role check (image-share-upload.controller.ts:135) does not cover CRDT writes, and there is no proxy/gateway in front of Yorkie in any config. The notes-side denial is purely client-side (editor.ts:443 EditorState.readOnly, :453-457 changeFilter), as the file's own comment at :431-437 concedes. Absence claim holds; in-lane (access control enforced only in the client) and blocking at major severity.

searchedFor: glob packages/notes/src/store/*.ts + grep readOnly there (no matches)
finding.summary: Read-only notes mounts are enforced only by `EditorView.editable`; the notes engine has no `EditorState.readOnly` and no read-only store wrapper, and this change widens that surface for viewer-role share links
finding.evidence: `initialize()` implements read-only as `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:425) plus hiding mutating API surface. `EditorState.readOnly` is never set (only in a test, checkbox-input.test.ts:87), and `noteSync` forwards ANY non-remote transaction carrying a `input`/`delete`/`move` user event straight to the store -> `YorkieNoteStore.editText()` -> Yorkie CRDT write (packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:57-100). There is no notes equivalent of `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts`, whose own doc comment states the reason this matters: "the server-side check behind it — the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one" (read-only.ts:35-42); the backend confirms the default (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101, self-hosting.md:185 `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE | false`). Vector: a visitor holding a *viewer*-role note share link opens the page and, from the console, dispatches into the mounted CodeMirror view (`EditorView.findFromDOM(...).dispatch({changes, userEvent:'input'})`) or calls the `NoteEditorAPI` mutators; noteSync writes it to the shared document, and in a stock deployment the webhook is in shadow mode so the server allows it. The change under review expands exactly this surface: `shared-notes-layout.tsx:117` now passes `onEditorReady={setEditor}` on the viewer mount (the old code passed none, so no external handle to the mutating API existed on that route) and the new view menu lets a viewer leave the preview-only pane for the editor pane (`shared-notes-layout.tsx:49-51,84-86`), which the previous code hard-pinned to `viewMode: "view"`. I could not find a *click-only* (no-devtools) write path in the read-only mount — the checkbox input checks `EditorView.editable` and the preview's `onToggleTask` is undefined when readOnly — hence medium rather than high confidence.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is wrong on both halves. (a) EditorState.readOnly IS set in production code: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:443 'EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)' inside initialize()'s extension list (EditorState imported at :6, state built at :483) — not only in checkbox-input.test.ts. (b) The notes engine DOES have the equivalent of packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts: editor.ts:453-457 installs, for read-only mounts only, EditorState.changeFilter.of((tr) => Boolean(tr.annotation(Transaction.remote))). A changeFilter returning false is applied inside EditorState.update(), so it strips the changes from ANY non-remote transaction — including the claimed console vector EditorView.findFromDOM(...).dispatch({changes,userEvent:'input'}) and every NoteEditorAPI mutator. Such a transaction never sets docChanged, and note-sync.ts:68 returns early on !update.docChanged, so store.editText() (note-sync.ts:96) is unreachable on a viewer mount; remote CRDT edits still apply because applyRemote tags them Transaction.remote (note-sync.ts:26-31). The only API write that bypasses the view, undo/redo calling store[kind]() directly, is refused at editor.ts:336-340, its keymap omitted at :352-353, and canUndo/canRedo hardwired false at :663-664; grepping store./getStore/getDoc in editor.ts shows no other store mutator and no exposed store handle, so there is no handle needing the docs-style Proxy wrapper. editor.test.ts:36-63 exercises exactly the configuration the finding says the change newly exposes (readOnly with viewMode 'edit'): editText and undo are never called after toggleBold/toggleTaskList/insertTable/insertCodeBlock/undo/redo, and :65-80 asserts remote changes still land. The write boundary the finding says is missing exists at the state level and is stronger than EditorView.editable.
